thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High GPU queue growth in eu-central1-primary. GPU util at 94%, request queue increasing, autoscaler errors detected (scale_limit_reached). Pager duty triggered for on-call.

Anne (on-call): On it, joining now. Any immediate customer-facing impact?

Miguel SRE: Seeing queue spike on inference-router and gpu-queue; jobs/sec up ~3x. Router is returning transient 429/504s for lower-priority routes. p99 latency jumping from 220ms -> 1.6s.

Lina (infra): Autoscaler logs show cloud provider returning quota_exceeded on attach requests. Also our config caps dedicated pool at max_pool_size 120; new requests hitting that ceiling.

Jordan (CSE): Multiple EU customers reporting slow responses and increased timeouts. One partner integration is retrying aggressively. Putting them on notice.

Anne (on-call): Ok. Plan proposals: 1) enable spillover to eu-west1 for non-SLA traffic, 2) pause low-priority batch jobs, 3) attempt emergency quota bump with provider, 4) notify impacted customers. Thoughts?

Ash (runtime): eu-west1 has warm model variants but mostly quantized smaller variants. Functional for most workloads but expect some quality differences. We can route best-effort traffic there. Need to ensure KV cache warming.

Tariq (netops): I can flip routing policy to allow overflow and set latency threshold. Will apply emergency policy with max_latency_ms 350 and spillover enabled.

Miguel SRE: Before cross-region routing, I'll pause the low-priority job scheduler to reduce new queue inflow. Also will throttle retries at the ingress to avoid thundering herd.

Anne (on-call): Lina, any ETA on quota increase? If provider queuing is long we must assume several minutes.

Lina (infra): I submitted emergency quota request to provider support; they accepted and queued but gave no firm ETA (est 15-45m). Meanwhile I bumped our internal dedicated pool config to 150 but autoscaler still blocked by provider side limit.

Tariq (netops): Applying routing change now. Command I ran:
```
rwdctl routing set --from eu-central1 --spillover eu-west1 --mode emergency --latency-threshold 350
kubectl patch configmap routing-policy -p 'spillover_enabled: true'
```
Routing policy applied, traffic should start shifting within ~30s.

Miguel SRE: Paused low-priority queue. Confirmed ingress retry window reduced to 3s. Queue length trending down: 18,200 -> 9,400 after 90s.

Ash (runtime): Started warming models in eu-west1 and enabling dynamic caching. Note: KV cache miss rate will spike; expect a temporary increase in token compute cost and latency for first requests.

Jordan (CSE): Drafting customer notification: "We've detected increased latency and throttling in eu-central1. We've enabled automatic spillover to eu-west1 to restore throughput; some requests may see small quality/latency changes. Working on capacity; updates soon." Posting to impacted customers now.

IncidentBot: Snapshot metrics: 'gpu_util_eu_central1: 94%', 'queue_size: 18200 -> 9400', 'p99_latency_ms: 1600 -> 420'.

Miguel SRE: After spillover and pause, queue down to 6,200 and p95 latency down from 850ms to 260ms. Throttling events reduced substantially.

Lina (infra): Provider accepted quota increase but provisioning delayed. We have a pending attachment; will keep monitoring. If provider attach completes, autoscaler should bring pool to requested size.

Anne (on-call): Good progress. Who's on comms? Jordan posted initial note. Add a follow-up in 15m.

Jordan (CSE): Follow-up posted to customers and status page. Included mitigation steps and ETA note: "monitoring for stabilization, next update in 20 minutes."

Ash (runtime): Noticed a small number of model fallback errors for enterprise routes that are pinned to higher-fidelity variants. I enabled pin-preserve policy for those routes (no spillover) to protect SLAs. That means some enterprise requests will remain queued until capacity returns.

Miguel SRE: Accepted risk. Low-priority and best-effort have been routed to eu-west1. Queue for enterprise-pinned routes stable but slowly rising; we'll keep an eye.

Tariq (netops): Routing policy log: 'spillover: enabled; overflow_target: eu-west1; excluded_routes: enterprise-sla; max_latency: 350ms'. No errors on config push.

Anne (on-call): Handoff plan: I'll stay on until we have stable p95 < 300ms and queue < 2k, then hand to next shift. Current status: queue 6.2k, p95 260ms, throttles dropping. Lina continue quota follow-up; Miguel keep pause until queue <2k.

Lina (infra): Provider reports attachments in progress. If attach completes, autoscaler will resume and should add GPUs to dedicated pool. Will post once confirmed.

Miguel SRE: If provider attach fails, fallback plan B: enable transient burst in cloud account (non-dedicated spot nodes) and auto-route best-effort traffic there. Need approval for cost.

Jordan (CSE): Customers acknowledging receipt; one asked for ETA on enterprise pinned queue — replied with "under active mitigation, we will not change enterprise routing; working on capacity increase."

Anne (on-call): Good. Creating concise runbook note in thread for handoff and tagging Sam on rotation. Final note before handoff: root cause appears to be simultaneous cloud quota exhaustion + config pool limit leading autoscaler to fail to grow. Mitigations: spillover, pause low-priority, emergency quota, and if needed burst to spot capacity.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Stabilization observed. Metrics trending: gpu_util_eu_central1 76%, queue 2.1k, p95 240ms.

Anne (on-call): Handing to daytime rotation — keep monitoring and reopen if regressions. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

Miguel SRE: A few follow-ups queued for postmortem: 1) add automated fallback to spot pool if quota errors on attach, 2) revisit pool max policy, 3) improve runbook around spillover thresholds.

Lina (infra): Noted. I'll coordinate quota pre-authorizations and talk to provider to secure higher soft limits for eu region.

Jordan (CSE): I'll follow up with impacted customers with final update once we confirm enterprise queue drained below threshold.

Ash (runtime): Will add KV cache warmers to reduce cold-start impact during future spillovers.

Tariq (netops): Leaving routing policy in emergency mode for 30m then revert to normal.

Anne (on-call): Thread summary posted to incident tracker. Closing incident channel in 10m if stable.
